### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s).

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via assertReferencesResolve (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 68 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3277c39e3726b8de7cf53aba3ef8aaf0f5fb862` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f8bc2c61b426c86575dc74216f4172923bdabbc3` — the merge of head `19624a54b92f9006003d99eb916f8b11dbb7ac34` into base `e3277c39e3726b8de7cf53aba3ef8aaf0f5fb862`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f8bc2c61b426c86575dc74216f4172923bdabbc3 && git checkout f8bc2c61b426c86575dc74216f4172923bdabbc3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3277c39e3726b8de7cf53aba3ef8aaf0f5fb862 19624a54b92f9006003d99eb916f8b11dbb7ac34 && git checkout -B drift-repro e3277c39e3726b8de7cf53aba3ef8aaf0f5fb862 && git merge --no-ff 19624a54b92f9006003d99eb916f8b11dbb7ac34

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3277c39e3726b8de7cf53aba3ef8aaf0f5fb862
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e3277c39e3726b8de7cf53aba3ef8aaf0f5fb862` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `19624a54b92f9006003d99eb916f8b11dbb7ac34`

Rendered by an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent that was fed the card, its thread and this PR only, and adopted by the `domain:engine#1` seat. Merge-base `c118524061`. `origin/main` was read at `2b52a5b013`; its `engine.ts` and `driver-sql/src/` are byte-identical to the merge-base. Three files, +432/−12.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Probe context: bare `{ isSystem: true }` → `ObjectQL.referenceCheckContext(context)`** (`{ ...(context ?? {}), isSystem: true }`). Both methods are private, and the package index is untouched: no export, type or wire-shape change. Right.
- **Newly refused:** a non-system write whose caller-supplied reference names a row stamped with an organization outside the caller's tenant scope. `buildDriverOptions` forwards `tenantId` (widened to `tenantIds` under `group`), and `SqlDriver.applyTenantScope` walls it with `OR organization_id IS NULL`. The refusal is the existing `reference_not_found`. Right.
- **Still accepted**, each resolved from the tree: tenancy-disabled objects, federated objects, NULL-organization rows, the `group` membership set, `systemFields.tenant: false` objects, the `single` posture, and a caller-held transaction. The spread keeps `context.transaction`, and `buildDriverOptions` prefers it over the ambient store the bare context used, so it is the same handle. Right.
- **RLS/FLS:** bypassed exactly as before. `isSystem: true` is written last in the spread, and the projection stays `['id']`. The dev measured this under the real `SecurityPlugin`. Right.
- **Oracle closure:** complete. The only callers of `assertReferencesResolve` are the insert, update-by-id and bulk-update doors, and `insertMany` delegates to `insert()`. The only other `referenceExists` caller is `inspectDanglingReferences`, which passes no context, so it stays byte-identical (pinned). Right.
- **Error surface:** unchanged — `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `fields[].code = 'reference_not_found'`, the documented shape. No new code. Right.
- **The `platformGlobalObjects` carve-out:** consistent, not a new regression. `buildDriverOptions` reads `isTenancyDisabled(schema)` alone, so an org-stamped row of a carve-out-only object is already unreadable to the caller (#15831, open). The probe now answers the same, and it self-corrects when one scope reaches the driver. Disclosed in the changeset. Right.
- **Reuse of `referenceCheckContext` / recording the elevation:** no new record owed. The recorded-elevation constraint belonged to the pre-delete check, which gained a NEW elevation. The write-path probe has run elevated since `20b1a9e67b`, and this PR narrows its tenant reach without changing its identity. `check-system-context-census` passes on the head.
- **Docblocks:** the "Why the probe is unscoped" section is replaced by the RLS-vs-tenancy distinction. `inspectDanglingReferences`' 「can never be more or less strict」 sentence is now false for the cross-organization class; it is out of region, see ③.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, with `Clause-②: no` and no arm, banner or marker → **right**. The PR automation's level rule keeps a `fix(` that changes no public surface at `patch`. `execution-duties.md` places a runtime security behaviour change outside clause ②. The `(narrowing)` kit is for shrinking the value domain of an authorable published key that a conforming author could have written and must now rewrite, and here nothing is authored or rewritten. A row in another organization was never in the documented accept set (`content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`, and the `isolated` posture's 「hard legal-entity wall」). Same-class precedent: PR #19800 (`a5afe382ba`, the same day) shipped `patch` with `Clause-②: no`, as did #16700 (`7ceb41672f`). Both changeset gates pass on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Audit scope (A/B/C)** → file separately. Shipped as A and pinned; B is the smallest restoration of the audit's promise, and it is out of region.
- **Master-detail parent-binding oracle** (`resolveMasterDetailParent` / `resolveMasterDetailParents` read the header under a bare `{ isSystem: true }`, and `evaluateValidationRules` runs before `assertReferencesResolve`) → file separately, p1 `security`: same class, same cure shape. **Does not block this PR.** It is a different read that predates the PR, and this PR narrows its outcome (open header: commit → `reference_not_found`). The update-path `readonlyWhen` leg is unmeasured.
- **`SummaryRecomputeError` after commit** → acceptable. It is now unreachable for non-system writes.
- **NOT MEASURED list** (REST/wire, live PG/MySQL, Turso, two prerequisite-exit-3 families) → acceptable. The fix sits in the engine above every driver, via `buildDriverOptions`, and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are green on the head.
- **Deviations** (a deleted scratch test, a deepened clone, a built dist) → acceptable; the head's tree is the three files.

Notes: the refusal tests assert `instanceof ValidationError`, `status: 400`, `code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED'` and `fields[].code` on all three doors, and the "elsewhere" and "nowhere" envelopes are deep-equal. The driver double is faithful to `applyTenantScope`; its only divergence is a literal `organization_id` key, which matters only for a renamed tenant column, and there is none in the fixture.
